text:
INDEPENDENT CHARACTERISATION. I did not file this bead; I tested the three hypotheses in its body separately. Two are ruled out and the third is confirmed and quantified.

FIRST, A DISCLOSURE. I had direct evidence of this and missed it. My coverage verification of the same function ran 600 calls and exceeded a 600-second timeout; I recorded "600 fits with analytic covariance is slow" and moved on, treating it as the honest cost of a new capability rather than as a finding. Whoever filed this bead was looking where I was not.

HYPOTHESIS 1 - ACCUMULATION LEAK. NOT REPRODUCED. Twelve sequential calls on one plan, q=2, 60 voxels, 60 nodes:

  per-call seconds   1.11 1.09 0.69 0.78 0.43 0.61 0.51 0.45 0.97 0.96 1.00 1.08
  mean first three 0.963 s, mean last three 1.016 s, ratio 1.05x
  correlation of call index with time  +0.084
  RSS 313 MB -> peak 373 MB -> 284 MB at the end, net MINUS 30 MB
  correlation of call index with RSS   +0.109

No time trend, and RSS falls back, which is garbage collection working rather than accumulation. This does not disprove a leak at 577 nodes with 50-voxel supports, but it does mean the leak is not a simple per-call accumulation and is not needed to explain the observation.

HYPOTHESIS 2 - COST DRIVEN BY CONDITION COUNT. RULED OUT. Eq. 13 is a D x D covariance over D = q(q-1)/2 distances, so the natural guess is that q=8 is expensive because D=28:

  q    D pairs   secs/node   secs per pair
  2          1       1.448          1.4477
  4          6       1.050          0.1749
  6         15       0.978          0.0652
  8         28       0.992          0.0354

Per-node cost is FLAT in q. At q=8 a node costs about 1.0 s here, not 7 s. So the 7 s/node in the field observation is not explained by q.

HYPOTHESIS 3 - PER-CALL WORK PROPORTIONAL TO THE WHOLE FRAME. CONFIRMED. Holding q=4 and holding mean support roughly constant, varying only the number of frame nodes:

  voxels   nodes   mean support   secs/node   vs first
  40          40            5.8       0.704       1.0x
  80          80            7.2       0.487       0.7x
  160        160            8.0       0.874       1.2x
  320        320            8.3       1.729       2.5x

From 80 to 320 nodes - a 4x increase - per-node cost rises 0.487 to 1.729, about 3.5x. Roughly linear in node count.

CONSEQUENCE, which is the actionable part: A FULL MAP SWEEP IS QUADRATIC IN NODE COUNT. N nodes each costing O(N) gives O(N^2). That reproduces the field observation without needing a leak at all. Extrapolating the slope to 577 nodes gives roughly 3 s/node before accounting for the larger 50-voxel supports, and 577 x 3 s is about half an hour, same order as the reported hour.

So the suspicion recorded in the bead body - "per-call recomputation of plan/fit-invariant work (residual factorization, contrasts, validation)" - is correct, and the recomputed work scales with the FRAME rather than being a fixed overhead. That is why single-node benchmarking missed it: at one node the redundant work is invisible, and it only becomes dominant as the frame grows.

CAVEATS, stated because I have over-claimed from timing twice today. This is synthetic data at 40-320 voxels with supports of 6-8 features, far smaller than 577 nodes at ~50 voxels. The extrapolation is approximate. The 80-node point is faster than the 40-node point, so there is real noise. And I did not attempt to identify WHICH invariant work is being redone - that needs profiling inside the call, which the implementer is better placed to do.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: profile one call at two frame sizes and diff the time by function. Whatever grows between them is the object that should be precomputed once and shared, which is the first fix shape the bead already proposes.
